scope_summary: Complete painting of interior door slabs (faces + edges) in new construction. Covers conditional primer coat, 2 finish coats, interstage sanding, and hardware handling. Separate from door frame/jamb (SF_DOOR_FRAME_NC) and door casing (SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT). Uses EA_SIDE as primary unit — each face is an independently paintable unit that may have different finish assignments. Fine Finish Doctrine governs all process and quality tier behavior.
relevant_findings: Doors are scrutinized surfaces — QT2 is not applicable per brief. QT3 minimum, QT4 default, QT5 for premium.
EA_SIDE is the atomic unit: each door face is independently assignable to a finish group. A door with 2 sides in different colors generates 2 separate line items.
Edge ownership convention: hinge edge → hinge side, latch edge → opening side (room you're standing in when door swings toward you). Top/bottom → shared or assigned to primary side.

Door type complexity factors per Doors Doctrine: flush=1.0, 2-panel=1.15, 4-panel=1.25, 6-panel=1.35, raised panel=1.4, french 10-lite=1.8, french 15-lite=2.2, bifold flush=0.7, bifold louvered=1.5, louver/closet=1.8
Factory primer is transit protection, not finish-ready primer — field primer is recommended for quality work (Doors Doctrine §2.2)
Fine Finish Doctrine interstage process is universal: inspect-repair-clean cycle runs between every coat at ALL quality tiers. What changes is scrutiny level, defect tolerance, and pace.
Spray is standard NC production method for doors. Brush for touch-up or occupied spaces.
Hardware removal is conditional on spray method — mask hinges (~5 min/hinge) or swap dummy hinges (~5 min/hinge) per Doors Doctrine §10
French doors require glass masking — adds 80-120% labor per Doors Doctrine §9.2 complexity modifiers
Louvered doors: 3 light spray coats preferred over 2 normal coats to manage drip risk on louver slats (Doors Doctrine §12.2)
Sanding grit progression per Doors Doctrine: QT3=no sand between coats, QT4=220 grit, QT5=320 grit
Material systems per Fine Finish Doctrine: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3), SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (QT4), SYS_FF_PREMIUM (QT5)
Sheen restrictions per Fine Finish Doctrine: QT3=satin or lower, QT4=any except gloss, QT5=any including gloss
Industry benchmarks per Doors Doctrine: flush door interior NC 2-coat = 3.60 man-hours total cycle, sprayed = 3.00 man-hours
Blocking prevention is critical for doors — use urethane-alkyd hybrids or water-based urethanes (Doors Doctrine §5.4)
Bifold doors use track system, not standard hinges — hardware removal is different
Door size affects SF per side: standard 6'8" ≈ 17.5 SF/side, tall 7'0"-8'0" ≈ 18.7-21.3 SF/side, oversized 8'0"+ > 21.3 SF/side

prep_requirements.method: Visual inspection for defects, factory primer condition assessment
prep_requirements.reason: Identify substrate defects, factory primer damage, and scope of prep work needed

prep_requirements.method: Dust removal, TSP wash if contaminated (high-touch surfaces)
prep_requirements.reason: Doors accumulate oils and construction dust. Contaminants cause fisheying or delamination.
Factory primer is transit protection — scuff for adhesion
prep_requirements.skip_conditions: Skip if bare wood (full sand instead)

prep_requirements.reason: Pre-hung doors may have nail holes from installation
prep_requirements.skip_conditions: Skip if no fastener holes present

prep_requirements.method: Shellac or oil-based sealer on cut MDF edges
prep_requirements.reason: MDF edges are porous — water causes swelling. Must seal before primer.

products: SW Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
limitations: Extended cure (7+ days for full hardness)

required_paintscope_keys.description: Total count of paintable door slab sides in scope
Count of bifold door panel sides

brief_proposed_door_sides.rationale: Catalog already has the correct key with EA_SIDE UOM. Brief's proposed key was a placeholder.

brief_proposed_doors_interior.rationale: Catalog has door opening count. Used for hardware removal/reinstall calculations.

zones_required.rationale: Door painting creates drips and overspray in immediate work area. Drop cloths under door being painted.
Spray creates overspray in door swing arc area. Protect floor in swing path.
Wall surfaces around door opening need protection from spray overspray.
Hinges and latch hardware must be masked or removed before painting.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Door slab meets frame at reveal. Same or different finish — two-tone doors exist. When same finish, slab and frame can be sprayed together. When different, masking required at reveal line.
Edges always match the face they are assigned to. Hinge edge → hinge side color. Latch edge → opening side color.

conditions_affecting_tasks.impact: Oversized/tall doors (8'0"+) may require step ladder for top portions. Standard doors accessed from floor.
Floor protection material selection. Finished floors need rosin paper. Subfloor may not need protection.

notes_for_materials_manager: Material systems follow Fine Finish Doctrine: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3), SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (QT4), SYS_FF_PREMIUM (QT5)
Coverage per door side: ~17.5 SF standard, ~21 SF tall, ~24+ SF oversized
Spray tip sizing: 310-411 for doors (fine atomization for smooth finish)
Blocking prevention critical — recommend urethane-modified products for all doors
MDF edge sealer needed as conditional consumable
Sanding supplies: 180 grit (prep), 220 grit (QT4 interstage), 320 grit (QT5 interstage)
Caulk/spackle for fastener holes and joint filling
notes_for_sop_librarian: Follow Fine Finish Doctrine module structure: Setup → Initial Prep → Prime (conditional) → Finish Coat → Interstage → Final Inspect → Cleanup
Interstage runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat (Fine Finish Doctrine §5.3)
Hardware removal/reinstall tasks conditional on spray method
Glass masking module required for french door_type
Louvered doors: 3 light coats instead of 2 standard coats per Doors Doctrine §12.2
Panel door application sequence: panels first → horizontal rails → vertical stiles → edges (PCA recommended, Doors Doctrine §8.1)
Edge painting: hinge edge matches hinge side, latch edge matches opening side
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Primary UOM is EA_SIDE — all rates expressed per door side
Door type complexity modifiers from Doors Doctrine §1.1: flush=1.0, panel_4=1.25, panel_6=1.35, french=1.8-2.2, bifold=0.7, louvered=1.8
Quality tier labor factors from Doors Doctrine §6.1: QT3=1.0, QT4=1.4, QT5=1.8
Industry benchmarks: flush door NC 2-coat = 3.60 man-hours total cycle (Doors Doctrine §9.1)
Spray vs brush: spray application ~15-20 min/door/coat vs brush 40-60 min/door/coat
Hardware removal: ~20 min/door (lockset + hinges). Reinstall: 10-20 min/door.
French door glass masking: ~80-120% additional labor over flush door baseline
Door size modifiers: standard=1.0, tall=1.1, oversized=1.25
assumptions: New construction doors — substrate condition is 'Good' (new or factory-primed)
Interior doors only — exterior faces excluded
Pre-hung doors installed by carpentry trade before paint scope
Two finish coats standard at all quality tiers (3 for louvered per Doors Doctrine)
Hardware is pre-installed or will be installed — hardware removal applies to spray method
Spray is standard NC production method; brush is alternate for specific conditions
uncertainties: Exact production rate per door side by type and method needs field calibration
Whether dummy hinge system is common enough to include as default vs masking
French door pane count variability (10-lite vs 15-lite) — use PS_META.EA.DOOR_PANES_TOTAL for precision
Bifold door track handling time variability
